_about: Hook formula library shared by reel-creator (writing), viral-researcher and performance-auditor (classifying). 'match' is a case-insensitive regex used to recognise the formula in existing hooks; it is a heuristic. Examples use {{placeholders}} wherever a real number or result would go: fill them with true facts or pick another formula.

families.contrarian: Challenges a belief the viewer holds. Earns attention through disagreement.
families.curiosity: Opens a gap the viewer wants closed.
families.story: Starts mid-event. Earns attention through a person and a moment.
families.proof: Leads with a result or a stake. Only usable with true numbers.
families.identity: Calls out exactly who this is for.
families.demo: Shows instead of tells. Hook is visual first.

formulas.name: The wrong default
formulas.example: Feeding your starter on a strict clock is wrong for home bakers.
formulas.use_for: Strong opinion you will defend in the comments.
formulas.avoid_when: You only half believe it. Rage-bait without a real argument gets hate-watched, not saved.

formulas.name: Swap the habit
formulas.example: Quit feeding your starter at midnight; a morning feed fits a work day.
formulas.use_for: Replacing one habit with a better one.
formulas.avoid_when: The habit is vague ('stop overthinking'). It must be a visible action.

formulas.name: Myth check
formulas.example: "Sourdough needs a whole weekend" isn't true. Here's a weeknight schedule.
formulas.use_for: A belief your audience repeats.
formulas.avoid_when: Nobody in your audience actually believes it.
formulas.match: \b(?:myth|isn'?t true|is not true|not actually true|that'?s false)\b

formulas.name: Learned the hard way
formulas.template: {Audience} learn this the hard way: {uncomfortable truth}.
formulas.example: Home bakers learn this the hard way: the fridge does most of the work.
formulas.use_for: An insider truth with a cost attached.
formulas.avoid_when: The truth is common knowledge in your niche.

formulas.name: The real reason
formulas.example: The real reason your loaf spreads flat is a starter fed too long ago.
formulas.use_for: Diagnosing a pain your audience has felt.
formulas.avoid_when: You cannot name the cause in the next sentence.
formulas.match: \b(?:the real reason|the actual reason|here'?s why|this is why)\b

formulas.name: What happens when
formulas.example: Here's what happens when you bake with a starter that peaked six hours ago.
formulas.use_for: Consequences of a choice viewers are weighing.
formulas.avoid_when: You have not actually seen it happen.

formulas.name: The one thing
formulas.example: The one step that stops your dough sticking to the basket.
formulas.use_for: A single, quotable fix.
formulas.avoid_when: It is really five things.

formulas.name: Mid-scene
formulas.example: Last March my starter grew a grey layer the night before a workshop.
formulas.use_for: A true moment with a turn coming.
formulas.avoid_when: The story has no turn. A diary entry is not a story.

formulas.name: Confession
formulas.example: I was wrong about feeding my starter every single night.
formulas.use_for: Credibility through admitting a mistake.
formulas.avoid_when: The 'mistake' is a humblebrag.

formulas.name: The experiment
formulas.template: I {kept doing one thing} for {time}. Here's how it went.
formulas.example: I kept my starter in the fridge for {{N}} weeks. Here's how it baked.
formulas.use_for: Experiments you actually ran.
formulas.avoid_when: You did not run it. Never invent the experiment.

formulas.name: What the mistake took
formulas.example: One wrong oven setting, and I lost {{N}} loaves in a single bake.
formulas.use_for: A real loss with a lesson.
formulas.avoid_when: You do not have the real number. Never estimate it on camera.

formulas.name: From / to
formulas.template: From {before state} to {after state}. One change.
formulas.example: From a dense brick to {{your result}} in one week. One change.
formulas.use_for: A verified transformation.
formulas.avoid_when: The after state is not verified.

formulas.name: Show the thing
formulas.template: Here's the {artifact} I actually use for {situation}.
formulas.example: Here's the exact bake schedule I used for {{N}} workday loaves.
formulas.use_for: Showing a real artifact on screen.
formulas.avoid_when: You cannot show it.

formulas.name: Numbered list
formulas.example: 3 signs that your starter is ready to bake with.
formulas.use_for: Save-worthy, list-shaped value.
formulas.avoid_when: The items are padding. Two great beats five fine.

formulas.name: How to, without
formulas.example: How to bake sourdough on a weeknight without staying up past ten.
formulas.use_for: Result plus the objection, in one line.
formulas.avoid_when: The 'without' is generic ('without stress').

formulas.name: Copy my template
formulas.example: Copy my feeding chart for the week your kitchen runs cold.
formulas.use_for: Templates, scripts, checklists.
formulas.avoid_when: There is nothing to copy.

formulas.name: Before you
formulas.example: Before you throw out your starter, try one warm feed.
formulas.use_for: A checklist moment right before a common action.
formulas.avoid_when: The check is obvious.

formulas.name: Name the viewer
formulas.example: If you're a home baker whose loaves spread flat, check your starter first.
formulas.use_for: Precise targeting; reaches fewer, converts more.
formulas.avoid_when: The person is broad ('if you're a creator').

formulas.name: POV
formulas.example: POV: your starter smells like nail polish the morning you planned to bake.
formulas.on_screen: POV: it smells like nail polish
formulas.use_for: Relatable skits and reactions.
formulas.avoid_when: The situation is not instantly recognisable to your audience.

formulas.name: Direct question
formulas.example: Bakers, do you feed your starter before or after work?
formulas.use_for: Starting an argument in the comments.
formulas.avoid_when: The answer is obvious.

formulas.name: Versus
formulas.example: Rye vs white flour starter: only one survives a cold kitchen.
formulas.use_for: Decisions your audience is stuck on.
formulas.avoid_when: You will not pick a side.

formulas.name: One-change demo
formulas.example: Same dough, one change: an extra night in the fridge.
formulas.use_for: Visual before/after you can show.
formulas.avoid_when: Nothing visibly changes on screen.

formulas.name: Object first
formulas.example: This plastic tub fixed my sticky dough.
formulas.use_for: A physical or on-screen thing as the hook.
formulas.avoid_when: The object is not on screen in the first second.

formulas.name: Save before
formulas.template: Save this for the next time {situation}.
formulas.example: Save this for the next time your starter stops rising.
formulas.use_for: Reference content people return to.
formulas.avoid_when: It is not something people will actually come back to.
